set.use: Diabetic CKD once proteinuria appears, and to slow CKD in general; avoid in stage 4-5 CKD and renal artery stenosis; guidelines often have them held before iodinated contrast
Calcium phosphate stones, alongside a low-sodium diet and a thiazide

set.mechanism: Chelating agents that bind cystine and help dissolve the stones
Extra buffer outside cells pulls H+ out in exchange for K+ moving in; used to alkalinize the urine (not the serum), so some toxins leave faster and some stones form less readily
